what_its_for: This combination birth control pill contains two hormones — a progestin (norethindrone) and an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol). It is used to prevent pregnancy. Some forms are also used to treat acne, reduce painful or heavy periods, or manage a condition called endometriosis. Talk to your doctor about all the reasons you are taking this medicine.
how_to_take: Take one pill by mouth every day, at the same time each day. Try to pick a time that is easy to remember, like when you brush your teeth in the morning or before bed. Swallow the pill whole with or without food. If the pill upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or at bedtime. Follow the order of pills in the pack exactly — do not skip pills or take them out of order. Most packs have 21 active (hormone) pills and 7 inactive (reminder) pills, or 28 active pills. Always start a new pack on time, even if your period has not ended yet.
dosing: Take one pill every day for 28 days, then start a new pack the very next day with no break. If your pack has 21 active pills and 7 reminder pills, take all 21 active pills, then take the 7 reminder pills, and start a new pack the next day. If your pack has all active pills (28 pills), take one daily with no break. Your doctor or pharmacist will tell you which type of pack you have and how to start. For the first month, you may need a backup method of birth control (like condoms) for the first 7 days unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
missed_dose: Missing pills increases your chance of getting pregnant. If you miss 1 pill: Take it as soon as you remember, even if that means taking 2 pills in one day. Then continue taking one pill per day as usual. No backup birth control is needed. If you miss 2 pills in a row in Week 1 or Week 2: Take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day. Then take 1 pill per day until you finish the pack. Use a backup method (like condoms) for the next 7 days. If you miss 2 pills in a row in Week 3, or miss 3 or more pills in a row at any time: Do not keep taking the missed pills. Throw away the rest of the pack and start a new pack that same day. Use a backup method for the next 7 days. You may not have a period that month. If you miss any reminder (inactive) pills, just throw them away and keep taking the rest of the pack. When in doubt, use a backup method and call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the pills in their original packaging. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use pills past the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not smoke, especially if you are over 35 years old. Smoking while taking this pill greatly increases your risk of serious heart problems such as blood clots, heart attack, and stroke. Avoid grapefruit juice in large amounts, as it may affect how the medicine works. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements. Some medicines can make your birth control less effective, including rifampin (an antibiotic), certain seizure medicines (like phenytoin or carbamazepine), and the herbal supplement St. John's Wort. Use a backup method of birth control if you start any new medicine. Limit alcohol, as it may increase side effects like nausea.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of these warning signs — use the word ACHES to help remember: Abdominal pain (severe stomach pain), Chest pain or shortness of breath, Headaches that are severe or sudden, Eye problems such as blurred vision or vision loss, Severe leg pain or swelling in one leg. Also call your doctor if you have: Signs of a blood clot (sudden leg swelling, redness, warmth, or pain), Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), A lump in your breast, No period for 2 months in a row or signs of pregnancy, Severe mood changes or depression, High blood pressure, Migraine headaches that are new or getting worse, or Any unusual or bothersome symptoms.
when_it_works: This pill works best when you take it every day at the same time without missing doses. For pregnancy prevention: It starts working right away if you begin taking it on the first day of your period. If you start on any other day, use a backup method like condoms for the first 7 days. For acne or period problems: It may take 3 to 6 months of regular use before you notice the full benefit. Give it time and keep taking it as directed.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking it, stop immediately and call your doctor. Breastfeeding: This pill is generally not recommended right after delivery or while breastfeeding, as it may reduce your milk supply. Talk to your doctor about safer birth control options while breastfeeding. Age: This medicine is not for use before the first menstrual period. It can be used by teenagers after puberty. Women over 35 who smoke should NOT use this medicine due to serious heart and blood clot risks. After menopause: This medicine is not used for menopause symptoms. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Diabetes: This medicine may slightly affect blood sugar. If you have diabetes, monitor your levels closely and tell your doctor.
